configuration: Both upstream cases of unittest/joint-translation.cpp. `vsFreeFlyer` builds a one-body translation robot and a one-body free-flyer robot, one body of mass 1 kg with its centre half a metre along the free flyer's x axis, at the literal all-ones configuration and velocity upstream itself writes. The SE3 and Motion operands of `spatial`, the Vector3::Random displacement it draws, and every literal of `vsFreeFlyer`, are read from ic/<ic>/operands.json.
observable: the translation joint's own transform and motion types, and the translation joint cross-validated against the first three columns and rows of a free-flyer model through forward kinematics, the composite subtree inertia, the nonlinear effects, the centre of mass, inverse dynamics, forward dynamics, the joint-space inertia and the joint Jacobian
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the model numbers and configurations, which upstream writes as literals, are read from ic/ at exactly those values, because the model and the configuration are themselves initial-condition inputs. Nothing is left out: both upstream cases are reproduced.
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero component of every frozen item in ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every component rather than one was measured, not assumed, on this leaf's cpp-joint-revolute: with a single component per item, 18 of cpp-explog's 48 observables and 6 of cpp-spatial's 76 came back with a spread of exactly zero, because a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one entry of a rotation matrix rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all nine. Every component still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this stays the generic two-ulp noise calibration rather than a physics experiment. A component that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 5.3291e-15 absolute. Two of this check's 26 observables, `translation_vs_freeflyer_jacobian_reference` and `translation_vs_freeflyer_jacobian_under_test`, show a spread of exactly zero and are insensitive by construction, not by accident: the translation joint's motion subspace is the constant 3-by-3 identity block of the local Jacobian's linear rows, independent of configuration, the same reasoning cpp-joint-revolute's own zero-spread local Jacobians rest on. Their bound therefore rests on the physical argument in the warrant rather than on a measured sensitivity.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the arithmetic is scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal, on 2026-09-14, x86_64, inside the env image: every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantities are the translation joint's own transform and motion types, and the translation joint cross-validated against a free-flyer model through forward kinematics, the composite subtree inertia, the nonlinear effects, the centre of mass, inverse dynamics, forward dynamics, the joint-space inertia and the joint Jacobian, in SI units and in the coordinate order the joint model or the spatial type fixes, which is part of the input and not something an implementation chooses. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 1.08e+01, it admits about 1.11e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a transposed motion subspace, a wrong block index in the free-flyer extraction (the translation joint's three degrees of freedom are the free flyer's first three columns, not any other three), a sign error in a cross product, or a dropped gravity term each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+1 in these units, seven to nine decades above the bound, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value of this check lands 9,755,437 times over it. Every upstream identity also stays active, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these expressions differs by about n eps |x|, roughly 40 * 2.2e-16 * 1.08e+01, which is decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 258 graded values by 5.3291e-15, using 5.112e-06 of the bound, that is 195,625 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
